items.summary: Oil fell as shipping through the Strait of Hormuz recovers, easing the war-risk premium built up after this week's US-Iran strikes -- a sign Middle East tensions are cooling.
Gold demand held steady as prices cooled, with central banks stepping up bullion purchases -- a sign institutional buyers see value even as retail interest softens.
BOJ held rates at 1% but warned core inflation may top its 2% target, keeping alive bets on a faster hike -- a yen-relevant signal for Asian markets.
China's factory activity unexpectedly contracted in July as the export rush that drove Q2 growth faded and typhoons hit output -- a warning sign for global demand.
US stock futures extended their rally as strong Big Tech earnings reignited the AI trade -- a bullish signal for risk appetite heading into the next trading session.
US borrowing costs hit a 19-year high even as the Fed held interest rates steady -- a sign bond markets are pricing in persistent inflation risk, not the cuts investors hoped for.
SK Hynix shares surged 25% and Samsung jumped over 20% as the AI-driven chip rally roared back -- a bellwether for global tech and Malaysia's own electronics exporters.
Gold surged nearly 2% to reclaim $4,100 after the Fed held rates steady and Middle East tensions flared -- underscoring gold's safe-haven pull whenever policy or geopolitical risk rises.
